provenance.what: The language-neutral oracle for a retained window body's pointer registry: an authored document tree + the window body it is painted into -> one registry entry per interactive node (control id, hit kind, dispatched action, absolute rect), and the entry a pointer point resolves to.
provenance.why: On the wgpu target the host's flat hit registry held the shell chrome and NOT ONE row of any retained window body: 31 targets, all chrome, so a pointer at (160.696, 138) — inside the published mounted_layout rect [0, 72, 315.392, 24] of the 'Add Generation' row — answered the WINDOW's HitKind::ScrollRegion. No row action dispatched, no NodeFlags::HOVERED was ever set, and a wheel over an engine surface never reached the scene. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, 📓️wgpu-runtime-mailbox-dispatch-2026-09-13.md §6.
provenance.rule: A registry entry's rect is the rect the retained paint drew that node at — one geometry, never a second derivation — and a body child is registered after the window's own ScrollRegion, so the reverse-order scan answers the child.

metrics.sharedWith: 🧫️fixtures/🌳️tree-row-rects/🔣️.json — the same one row metric layout, paint and this registry all read

rules.oneGeometry: Every entry's rect is the absolute rect the retained paint walk painted that node at: the walk's accumulated parent origin plus the node's own published mounted_layout rect, minus a scrollable ancestor's live scroll offset. A registry that derives its own rectangles is the defect this fixture pins.
rules.order: The window's own ScrollRegion is registered before its body paints; every body entry follows it, and the registry is scanned in reverse, so a body entry always outranks the window beneath it. Within a body, entries follow the paint walk's pre-order, so a child outranks its parent.
rules.treeItem: A tree item row registers HitKind treeItem under 'tree.label.<item id>', dispatching that row's own activate action. Its band is exactly one rowHeightPx even when the row's published height also covers the nested rows it reveals — each nested row registers its own band.
rules.treeSection: A labelled tree section row registers HitKind treeItem under 'section.chevron.<section id>' over its header band of one rowHeightPx. An unlabelled section has no header band and registers nothing.
rules.button: A Button registers HitKind button under its own id, dispatching its action. A Stack that carries an activate action and is not a tree row registers the same way.
rules.input: An Input registers HitKind input, a Select select, a Toggle toggle, a Slider slider, a NumberStepper numberStepper, a Ring ring and an IconSelect iconSelect — each under the node's own id, with no dispatched action: the retained event router owns what a press on those means (🧫️fixtures/🎛️retained-control-commit/🔣️.json is what it means). The last three registered NOTHING before ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, so a press on a generation's stepper, ring or icon field resolved the WINDOW beneath it.
rules.engineSurface: A world-3d surface canvas registers HitKind world3d under its surface id. Every other bespoke-dispatch surface reuses the scrollRegion + '.pane' / '.map' convention the shell's scroll_region_is_scene_surface already reads, so a wheel over one propagates to the scene instead of scrolling the window that hosts it.
rules.container: A plain container (a Stack with no activate, a Section, a Group, a Field), a Text, a Separator and a Tree's own frame register nothing — they are pass-through, and the pointer falls to whatever is registered beneath them.
rules.zeroArea: An entry with no area is never registered: a mounted-but-unplaced node must not take the pointer from the node drawn there.
